newsitem.title: USA: Universal Forest on track to meet '97 goals.
newsitem.headline: Universal Forest on track to meet '97 goals.

text.p: Universal Forest Products Inc said Monday it is on target to reach its previously stated goal of increasing earnings 10 percent to 15 percent in 1997.
The maker of wood products for the do-it-yourself retail and manfuactured housing markets posted second quarter earnings of $9 million or $0.51 a share, versus $8.2 million or $0.46 a share.
For the first six months of this year, the company had earnings of $12.3 million or $0.69 a share, up from $10.8 million or $0.61 a share.

"At the halfway point of 1997, we have made considerable progress in achieving many of our strategic goals for growing Universal. We are on-track for a strong year in revenues and earnings," William Currie, chief executive officer, said in a statement.

Second quarter sales were up 24 percent to $341.3 million, which Universal attributed to higher unit volume and lumber price increases. However, margins were down from last year because of the higher lumber prices and continuing competitive pricing pressure in the company's manufactured housing business.
